s1.syndrome_frame: Palpitations and syncope in a patient with complex congenital heart disease
salient_findings: Tachycardia with heart rate of 183 bpm
Irregularly irregular tachycardia with grouped beating on ECG
key_facts: Patient has complex congenital heart disease with D-transposition of the great arteries
Patient has single ventricle physiology with a large ventricular septal defect
Patient has Fontan circulation
Patient experiences lightheadedness and syncope while walking
Patient has been prescribed diltiazem and apixaban
ECG shows irregularly irregular tachycardia with grouped beating
Transesophageal echocardiogram shows no intracardiac thrombus
Patient's heart rate is 183 bpm in the emergency department
Diltiazem administration converts tachycardia to regular narrow complex tachycardia
Adenosine administration induces temporary heart block with continuation of supraventricular tachycardia

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG shows irregularly irregular tachycardia with grouped beating and intermittently visible P waves, which is consistent with intra-atrial reentrant tachycardia, a common arrhythmia in patients with complex congenital heart disease and Fontan circulation.

rejected.label: Orthodromic atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia
rejected.why: The ECG does not show a consistent pattern of retrograde P waves, which is typical of orthodromic atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia.

rejected.label: Atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia
rejected.why: The response to adenosine, which induced temporary heart block with continuation of supraventricular tachycardia, is not typical of atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia.

rejected.label: Supraventricular tachycardia with aberrancy
rejected.why: The ECG does not show a clear pattern of aberrancy, and the response to diltiazem and adenosine is not consistent with supraventricular tachycardia with aberrancy.

rejected.label: Atrial fibrillation
rejected.why: The ECG shows a more organized rhythm with grouped beating, which is not typical of atrial fibrillation.
